newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil seen 25-50 cts down, Brent flat-5 ct off.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil seen 25-50 cts down, Brent flat-5 ct off.

text.p: IPE May gas oil was called to open $0.25 to $0.50 a tonne lower on Tuesday while June Brent was expected to open unchanged to five cents a barrel down.

"Brent is due about five (cents a barrel) down, $18.23 is the level I am looking for at the opening. Gas oil, 50 cents down, it may not even meet that call and only come a quarter (of a dollar) down, basically holding the low of $165 yesterday on the opening," one broker said.
May gas oil closed 25 cents up at $165.75 on Monday while June Brent closed flat at $18.27.

Brokers said the market, which had a lacklustre performance on Monday, was range-bound and needed a fresh injection of fundamental news, like weekly American Petroleum Institute inventory data, due on Tuesday night.
We had the Shell news which obviously supported the crude a little bit but it did not give the market enough momentum to move," a broker said.
Shell Nigeria said on Monday it would restart normal production from Forcados after reaching agreement with local communities to reopen oil flow stations shut at the weekend.
Shell said on Friday that 20 percent of its 475,000 barrels per day (bpd) Forcados output was shut in by closures as a result of ethnic clashes in the oil-producing Niger delta.

"On the upside $20 continues to be good resistance for WTI, so we are range bound and we need a fresh injection on news, possibly the APIs tonight, possibily the products expiry tomorrow will give us a little bit more direction," the broker added. -- Haitham Haddadin, London newroom +44 171 542 8145
